item.title: 墨西哥2027年经济增长率高达2.5%,2027年预算草案赤字较小。
item.author: By Natalia Siniawski and Adriana Barrera
item.description:
本地机器翻译 · 原文附后

由娜塔莉娅·西尼awski和阿德里亚娜·巴雷拉主演

墨西哥城,9月8日(路透社)——墨西哥财政部预测,2027年的经济增长在1.5%-2.5%之间,而根据星期二提交国会的概算草案,更广泛的公共部门赤字将缩小到国内生产总值的3.9%。

• 预算文件显示,2026年的增长估计数为1.0%至2.0%,从先前的1.8%降至2.8%。

• 公共部门赤字占预计2026年国内生产总值的4.1%。

· 2027年的前景主要取决于坚实的国内需求、较高的家庭收入、较少限制的财政条件,以及与“墨西哥计划”倡议下的基础设施项目和税收奖励有关的投资。

• 预期北美贸易一体化支持的出口增长会提供更多支助。

· 根据《公共部门借款要求的历史平衡》(SHRFSP)衡量,2027年公债总额达到国内生产总值的55.0%,而2026年年终估计为54.0%。

• 根据墨西哥银行的官方目标,头条通货膨胀预计将以3.0%完成2027年。

• 邦石油公司Pemex公司预计将从联邦政府收到811亿墨西哥比索(48.0亿美元),以偿还2027年的债务,而前一预算为2635亿比索。

政府也为Pemex的优先投资项目拨款2555亿比索。

• 宏观经济框架假定墨西哥的原油出口组合在2027年平均每桶61.80美元,低于2026年每桶78.40美元。

• 液体碳氢化合物总产量预计为每天180万桶。 (1美元=16.9062墨西哥比索)

(由阿德里亚娜·巴雷拉和娜塔莉娅·西尼亚夫斯基报道;由安东尼·埃斯波西托编辑)

原文：Mexico sees up to 2.5% economic growth in 2027, narrower deficit in 2027 budget draft

By Natalia Siniawski and Adriana Barrera

MEXICO CITY, Sept 8 (Reuters) - Mexico's finance ministry projects economic growth of between 1.5% ‌and 2.5% in 2027, while the broader public sector deficit ‌is forecast to narrow to 3.9% of gross domestic product (GDP), according to a draft budget proposal submitted to Congress on Tuesday.

• The budget document shows a 2026 growth estimate of 1.0% to 2.0%, down from an earlier projection of 1.8% to 2.8%.

• The public sector deficit compares to 4.1% ‌of GDP projected for ⁠2026.

• The 2027 outlook is driven primarily by solid domestic demand, higher household incomes, less restrictive financial ⁠conditions, and investment tied to infrastructure projects and tax incentives under the "Plan Mexico" initiative.

• Additional support is expected from export growth backed by North American trade integration.

• Total public debt, as measured by the Historical Balance ‌of Public Sector Borrowing Requirements (SHRFSP), is seen reaching 55.0% of GDP in 2027, compared with 54.0% estimated for year-end 2026.

• Headline inflation is projected to finish 2027 at 3.0%, in line with the Bank of Mexico's official target.

• State oil firm Pemex is slated to ‌receive 81.1 billion Mexican pesos ($4.80 billion) from the federal government to pay down debt in 2027, compared with 263.5 billion pesos in the prior budget. The ‌government also earmarked 255.5 billion pesos for Pemex's priority investment projects.

• The macroeconomic framework assumes Mexico's crude export mix will average $61.80 per barrel in 2027, down from an estimated $78.40 per barrel in 2026.

• ‌Total liquid hydrocarbon production is projected at 1.80 million barrels per day.($1 = 16.9062 Mexican pesos)

(Reporting by Adriana Barrera and Natalia Siniawski; Editing by Anthony Esposito)
